clue.text: Queen possibly grasping simple form of entertainment

indicators.note: grasping means one word holds the other tightly inside it

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so 'possibly' flags that a queen is one example of a cat
simple means bare, plain and unadorned

explanation.surface: A monarch apparently clutching some unsophisticated kind of show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' points at royalty, but a queen is also a female cat; 'grasping' puts the second piece inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is a style of nightclub entertainment with song, dance and comedy.

clue.text: A man under roof of chapel is plastering

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming lower in the column, so after
in a down entry the roof is the top, so the opening letter of chapel is taken

parts.note: a king is a chess man, one of the pieces on the board

explanation.surface: Someone working beneath a chapel roof is busy with the plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a chess piece here, the KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Caking means coating thickly, as with plaster or mud covering a surface.

clue.text: Brahms and Liszt for starters, German is sozzled

indicators.note: starters are the opening course, so the first letters of the two composers are taken

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: Two composers to begin with, and a German getting very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brahms and Liszt' is British rhyming slang for drunk (pissed), a joke on the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely drunk, a close synonym of sozzled.

clue.text: Vessel beneath reddish-brown banger

indicators.note: in a down entry the vessel sits lower in the column, after the colour

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour
a bucket is a vessel for carrying liquid

explanation.surface: A container below a reddish-brown old car.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a battered old car, not a sausage here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms are slang for a decrepit old car in poor condition.

clue.text: Complete wreck

definitions.meaning: complete as an adjective means entire, whole
to wreck a car thoroughly is to write it off as a ... loss (chiefly American slang)

explanation.surface: A thorough wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Total is an adjective meaning entire and a verb meaning destroy a vehicle beyond repair.

clue.text: Drawings, quite a few on back of card

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the oodles come after
the back of a word is its final letter, so the end of card is taken

parts.note: oodles means lots, quite a few

explanation.surface: Plenty of sketches scribbled on the reverse of a card.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodles are idle drawings or scribbles made absent-mindedly.

clue.text: Give pair of lines love as an artist

parts.note: to donate is to give
L is the abbreviation for line, so two of them are LL
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand over two lines with affection, in the manner of a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Donatello was an Italian Renaissance sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was a Florentine sculptor, a classic example of an artist.

clue.text: Artist shaving head for god

indicators.note: to shave the head is to remove the top, so the initial letter of the sculptor is cut off

parts.note: Auguste Rodin was a French sculptor

explanation.surface: A painter getting a haircut to look like a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Note zigzagging lines under rim, as artist

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means lower in the column, so the note and lines follow the rim

parts.note: a lip is the rim of a vessel
a chit is a short note or memo
the letter Z is drawn as a zigzag of three lines

explanation.surface: A musical note waving about below the edge, in an artistic way.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Lipchitz was a Cubist sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipchitz was a Lithuanian-born French sculptor, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Classic marks arising for artist

indicators.note: in a down clue, arising means reading upwards, so both pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: trad means traditional, classic (as in trad jazz)
dots are small marks

explanation.surface: Traditional marks coming up for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Stoddart is a Scottish neoclassical sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoddart is a contemporary Scottish sculptor, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Gesture of defiance contrary for artist

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to cock a snook is a rude gesture of defiance, thumb on nose

explanation.surface: A painter making a rude gesture the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeff Koons is an American artist known for balloon-animal sculptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Koons is a celebrated American sculptor and painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Prison reforms attributed to figure in racketeer?

indicators.note: attributed to means attached to, so the number and the rearranged word are joined

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number

indicators.note: reforms means remakes, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prison reforms credited to a key figure in organised crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racketeer' suggests a gangster; with the question mark it is someone who wields a racket for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional tennis player plays with a racket, a playful reading of racketeer.

clue.text: A word of gratitude in the peerage for eminence

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the thanks goes inside the peerage

parts.note: the peerage is the nobility, the titled class
ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: Thanking the aristocracy for their distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Notability and eminence are synonyms for distinction and fame.

clue.text: Builder's trough — oops, it's fallen over!

indicators.note: something fallen over is upside down, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: d'oh is an exclamation on making a blunder, like oops

explanation.surface: A builder's container topples and he cries out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hod is a trough on a pole used by builders to carry bricks.

clue.text: Slotting in money initially, turn a load around — here?

definitions.text: Slotting in money initially, turn a load around — here?

indicators.note: slotting in means putting a piece inside, so the letter goes into the rearranged letters
around means turned about, so these letters are rearranged
initially means the first letter of money is taken

explanation.surface: Put coins in the slot and spin a wash: where would you be?
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges TURN A LOAD into LAUNDROAT, and 'Slotting in' puts M inside it. The whole clue also describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A launderette is where you feed coins into machines and spin a load of washing.

clue.text: Fish joining stream after swimming instructor

indicators.note: joining means the two pieces are put side by side

parts.note: a school is a group of fish swimming together

indicators.note: swimming means moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fish entering a stream after its swimming coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' looks like the fish's activity but is the anagram signal; 'after' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is a male teacher, a synonym of instructor.

clue.text: Short of bees, audibly, lob rosebuds away — as not humming?

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so these letters are taken out of the pool
away suggests the letters are knocked about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: bees sounds like B's, two letter B

explanation.surface: Bees gone, a gardener knocks rosebuds off: no buzzing now?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' takes BB from LOB ROSEBUDS and 'away' rearranges what is left. 'humming' is British slang for smelly, not buzzing.
explanation.definitionFit: Humming is British slang for smelling bad, so lacking any smell is a witty sense.

clue.text: The value of cool artist

parts.note: hep is dated slang for cool, fashionable
worth means value

explanation.surface: What being cool is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Hepworth was an English modernist sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepworth was a major British sculptor, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Too much to raise in dollars for the seated area

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the excess goes inside the dollars

parts.note: bucks is slang for dollars

indicators.note: in a down clue to raise is to lift upward, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, too much

explanation.surface: Raising an excessive sum in dollars to pay for the seating.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttocks are the body part one sits on, humorously the seated area.

clue.text: Each clue needs one dog trained to find the scent

indicators.note: trained means shaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Every clue requires a trained dog to sniff out the trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scent' suggests a dog's trail, but it is a perfume. 'trained' rearranges CLUE ONE DOG into UDECOLOGNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a light perfume, a kind of scent.

clue.text: Kandinsky originally a substandard artist

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: poor means substandard

explanation.surface: Kandinsky was once a poor artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Anish Kapoor is a British-Indian sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Kapoor is a well-known sculptor, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Judge is introduced to magistrate finally, when standing

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing means upright, so the pieces read upwards, backwards

parts.note: meets means is introduced to

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of magistrate

explanation.surface: A judge is presented to a magistrate at last, while rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is a verb here, not the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem is to regard or consider, an old sense of judge.

clue.text: Card and cut

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: with means and, together with

explanation.surface: A card that has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' suggests the deck, but means a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is a witty, amusing person, as is a wit.

clue.text: Meeting of Ford and British colonialist reported as a turning point

parts.note: to ford a river is to cross it

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so the colonialist's name gives its sound-alike

parts.note: Cecil Rhodes was a British imperialist in southern Africa

explanation.surface: A carmaker and an empire-builder meet at a decisive moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like the car maker but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossroads is figuratively a critical moment of decision, a turning point.

clue.text: African lover endlessly cuddles Zambian leader

indicators.note: cuddles means holds close, so one piece goes inside
endlessly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a swain is a lover or suitor

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the initial letter is taken

explanation.surface: A boyfriend constantly hugs the Zambian president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' turns SWAIN into SWAI, and 'cuddles' puts Z inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swazi is a person from Eswatini (Swaziland), an African.

clue.text: Comfortable seat, up until now, finally lost

indicators.note: the final letter is lost, so it is removed

parts.note: so far means up until now

explanation.surface: A cosy chair, which up to now has finally gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally lost' drops R from SO FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people.

clue.text: Time when You'll Never Walk Alone was sung by legendary giant in musical show

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces stand next to each other

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

parts.words: You'll Never Walk Alone was sung
parts.note: the Kop is the stand at Liverpool's Anfield where the fans sing this anthem
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A football anthem sung by a mythical giant, during a stage performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kop is the famous terrace at Liverpool FC's ground, whose fans sing You'll Never Walk Alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock opera is a musical stage work in rock style, a musical show.

clue.text: Dock strike's ending for artist

parts.note: to moor a boat is to dock it

indicators.note: the ending is the final letter of strike

explanation.surface: The end of a dockers' strike, for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Moore was an English sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Moore is one of Britain's best-known sculptors, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Old cavalrymen back in South America, a hundred escaping injuries

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so the end of South is taken

parts.note: US is short for the United States, America

indicators.note: escaping means getting out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: scars are marks left by injuries
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Former horse soldiers home in South America, a hundred dodging wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back in South America' suggests a reversal or SA; it is the last letter of South plus US for America.
explanation.definitionFit: Hussars were light cavalry soldiers, originally from Hungary.

clue.text: Meanwhile, waste time in middle of performance

indicators.note: to waste is to wreck or ruin, so these letters are rearranged
the middle of an eleven-letter word is its sixth letter, so the centre of performance is taken

explanation.surface: Meanwhile, someone kills time partway through a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waste time' reads as idling, but 'waste' rearranges TIME, IN and R, the centre of 'performance'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the interim is an idiom meaning in the meantime, so the word alone stands for meanwhile.
